title: Wan2.1 official README
claims: The official Wan2.1 README states that T2V-1.3B requires 8.19 GB VRAM and can generate a 5-second 480P video on an RTX 4090 in about 4 minutes without quantization.
Wan2.1 T2V-14B supports 480P and 720P; T2V-1.3B is listed for 480P and the README warns that 720P is less stable because of limited high-resolution training.
The Diffusers example uses 81 frames at 16 fps, guidance scale 5, and UniPC flow shift 5 for 720P or 3 for 480P.
For the 1.3B command the README gives sample guide scale 6 and sample shift 8–12.

resources.gpu: RTX 4090 for the timing claim; VRAM floor is model-author stated
resources.workflow: Wan2.1 official generate.py or Diffusers WanPipeline/WanImageToVideoPipeline

limitations: The 8.19GB and 4-minute figures are not L4 or A100 measurements; the README does not provide host RAM or peak VRAM for the 14B paths.

title: Wan2.2 official README
claims: Wan2.2 A14B uses high-noise and low-noise experts, each about 14B parameters; only one expert is active per denoising step.
The high-noise expert is used early and the low-noise expert is selected when t is below the SNR-derived t_moe threshold.
The official single-GPU T2V/I2V A14B command is labeled as requiring at least 80GB VRAM; --offload_model, --convert_model_dtype and --t5_cpu are listed as OOM mitigations.
TI2V-5B supports 1280x704/704x1280 720P at 24fps and is labeled runnable on a GPU with at least 24GB VRAM with offload/dtype/T5 CPU flags.
The official authors state that TI2V-5B can generate a 5-second 720P video in under 9 minutes on a single consumer-grade GPU without specific optimization.

resources.gpu: Official A14B command: at least 80GB; official TI2V-5B command: 24GB class
resources.precision: Official BF16/config dtype path; --convert_model_dtype is a dtype cast, not 4-bit quantization

limitations: The under-9-minute statement does not identify a specific GPU, peak VRAM, host RAM, frame count, or exact step count; official A14B 80GB wording is a command-level floor, not a measured L4 result.

title: ComfyUI official Wan2.2 14B T2V workflow template
claims: The template links FP8-scaled high-noise and low-noise T2V experts at 13.31GB each, Wan2.1 VAE at 242.1MB, and UMT5 FP8-scaled text encoder at 6.27GB.
The template links Wan2.2 T2V Lightning v1.1 high-noise and low-noise LoRAs at 1.14GB each.
The default latent is 640x640x81; output FPS is 16 and duration proxy is 5 seconds.
Base mode defaults to 20 steps split 10/10 with CFG 3.5; Lightning mode uses 4 steps split 2/2 with CFG 1.0; both use Euler/simple and ModelSamplingSD3 shift 5.
The template note records an RTX4090D reference: FP8-scaled at 640x640 used 84% VRAM and about 536s first/513s second run; FP8-scaled plus 4-step LoRA used 89% and about 108s first/71s second run.

resources.gpu: RTX4090D for the embedded reference note; not an L4/A100 measurement
resources.precision: FP8-scaled experts and text encoder; Wan2.1 VAE

limitations: The RTX4090D note is retained as source-condition evidence only and is not extrapolated to L4; the template does not report host RAM or quality metrics.

title: Wan2.2-Lightning model-author README
claims: The author describes Wan2.2 Lightning as a distilled model requiring 4 steps without the CFG trick and claims approximately 20x speed-up.
T2V V1.1 and I2V V1 high/low LoRA pairs have Native Comfy and Kijai wrapper workflow JSON files.
V2.0/0928 updates are described as improving camera controllability and motion dynamics; the model-author README links comparison MP4s and demo MP4s.
The author explicitly reports a limitation: extremely large motion can create artifacts and vehicle direction can be reversed.

resources.precision: LoRA with base Wan2.2 high/low experts; native and quantized variants elsewhere in LightX2V
resources.workflow: Wan2.2 official generate.py with lora_dir; Native Comfy or Kijai workflow

limitations: The x20 claim has no L4/A100 timing row; the author quality claim is not a controlled full/base paired metric and the README preserves motion/artifact counterexamples.

title: LightX2V model structure and Wan2.1-14B guide
claims: LightX2V lists separate Wan2.1 and Wan2.2 LoRA repositories; Wan2.2 requires separate high-noise and low-noise LoRA entries.
The Wan2.1 4-step config uses infer_steps 4, denoising list [1000,750,500,250], sample_shift 5, sample_guide_scale 6, enable_cfg false, and LoRA strength 1.0.
The guide explains that enable_cfg=true runs positive and negative prompts separately, increasing inference time; CPU offload and model-level offload reduce VRAM.
LightX2V lists Wan2.1 BF16/FP8/INT8 4-step files and Wan2.2 high/low BF16/FP8/INT8 4-step files; it describes original BF16 size about 28.6GB and FP8/INT8 about 15GB in the Wan2.2 Distill README.

resources.gpu: Guide timing rows are H100; model docs name 80GB+ and 24GB+ configuration classes
resources.precision: BF16 original; FP8 or INT8 quantized DIT; `fp8-vllm`/`int8-vllm` schemes

limitations: The H100 timings in the linked guide are outside the requested L4/A100 scope; the docs establish file/config contracts but not a low/mid quality comparison.

title: LightX2V benchmark source for Wan2.1 I2V
claims: The H200 480P test uses Wan2.1-I2V-14B, 40 steps, seed 42, CFG enabled; official 366s/71GB is compared with LightX2V distill 14s/35GB.
The H200 720P test uses 40 steps, seed 1234, CFG enabled; official 974s/81GB is compared with LightX2V distill 44s/43GB.
The RTX4090 480P test reports LightX2V distill 63–68s with 12–16GB GPU memory; 720P distill 171–183s with 18–23GB.
The benchmark says all rows use 81 output frames and documents FP8, offload, TeaCache threshold 0.2, and distilled CFG disabled.

resources.gpu: H200 and RTX4090 only; no L4/A100

limitations: H200/RTX4090 are outside the requested direct L4/A100 hardware scope; no visual metric or same-hardware L4/A100 comparison is reported.

title: CausVid official repo and Wan causal DMD config
claims: The official repo uses Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B as the base model and gives autoregressive 3-step 5-second and bidirectional 3-step 5-second inference commands.
The repo's data preparation converts videos to 480x832x81 at 16fps.
The causal DMD config lists timestep_shift 8.0, real_guidance_scale 3.5, denoising_step_list [1000,757,522,0], and num_frame_per_block 3.
The paper/repo claims 9.4 FPS streaming generation on one H100 with KV caching, but this is outside L4/A100 scope.

resources.gpu: H100 for the 9.4 FPS author claim
resources.precision: mixed precision in training config; inference checkpoint details not hardware benchmarked

limitations: No L4/A100 inference timing, VRAM peak, host RAM, or controlled visual comparison is provided; training config guidance scale is not a guaranteed Comfy inference CFG setting.

title: Wan2.1-T2V-14B-CausVid model card
claims: The card describes Wan2.1-T2V-14B-CausVid as a Wan2.1 14B foundation with causal diffusion and a 9-step distillation process.
The training data used about 15,000 OpenSora prompt-video pairs with 81 frames each.
The inference framework is LightX2V; num_fragments controls approximately 5-second autoregressive video segments.
limitations: No low/mid GPU benchmark, peak memory, host RAM or output quality comparison is reported in the card.

title: TurboDiffusion official README
claims: TurboDiffusion provides checkpoints for Wan2.1 T2V-1.3B/14B and Wan2.2 I2V-A14B; its README states unquantized checkpoints are for GPUs above 40GB and quantized checkpoints plus --quant_linear for RTX4090/5090-class cards.
Wan2.1 runner supports 1–4 sampling steps, default 4, sigma_max 80, SageSLA top-k default 0.1, and quantized linear layers when using quant checkpoints.
Wan2.2 I2V runner supports 1–4 steps, default 4, sigma_max 200, high/low boundary default 0.9, SageSLA top-k default 0.1, and an optional ODE mode described as sharper but less robust than SDE.
The published evaluation is on a single RTX5090: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B-720P E2E diffusion 38s; Wan2.1 T2V-1.3B-480P 1.9s; Wan2.1 T2V-14B 720P 24s; 480P 9.9s.

resources.gpu: RTX5090 for all published evaluation rows; >40GB guidance mentions H100
resources.time_s: 38/1.9/24/9.9 E2E diffusion seconds by listed model
resources.precision: W8A8/quantized linear path for <=40GB; unquantized path for >40GB

limitations: No L4 or A100 run is reported; 5090 speed and quality claims cannot be transferred directly to requested hardware. README says checkpoints/paper are not finalized and prompts are trained on long English prompts.

title: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-Turbo model card and few-step config
publisher: Quanhao Li et al. / MagicMotion contributors
claims: The model is distilled from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B using step distillation and CFG distillation; it is a 4-step model with no CFG trick.
The author card states output support of 121 frames at 24fps and 1280x704, for both T2V/I2V unified TI2V usage.
The public inference script uses h=704, w=1280, num_frames default 121 and exports at 24fps; the public config lists denoising_step_list [1000,750,500,250] and warp_denoising_step=true.
The author says the training run was 4000 iterations under 48 hours on a cluster of 16 A100 GPUs.
limitations: The 16-A100 figure is training hardware, not single-A100 or L4 inference; no inference wall time, peak VRAM, host RAM, or quality A/B is reported.

title: vLLM-Omni Wan2.2 T2V-A14B serving performance
claims: The test environment is one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB with FlashAttention.
Dataset A is 854x480, 80 frames, 16fps, 3 inference steps; mean latency is 24.6766s with VAE parallel 1 and 21.6810s with VAE parallel 4, CFG parallel 2, Ulysses 2, HSDP on.
Dataset B is 1280x720, 80 frames, 16fps, 6 inference steps; mean latency is 124.6639s with VAE parallel 1 and 117.44s with VAE parallel 4 under the same parallel settings.
The benchmark defines mean and P99 HTTP latency and concurrency 1.

resources.gpu_count_evidence: Main inference from CFG parallel 2 x Ulysses 2 x TP 1 and official GPU-count formula; benchmark page does not explicitly list total devices.
resources.resource_scope: high-resource multi-GPU reference, excluded from single-A100 evidence

limitations: This is a serving implementation with Ulysses/CFG/VAE parallelism and HSDP, not the official single-GPU generate.py path; host RAM and visual quality metrics are absent. Main primary-source check: CFG=2 and Ulysses=2 imply four GPUs under official parallel-degree constraints, not one A100. Low-step throughput table has no corresponding quality acceptance evidence.

title: Wan2.2 TI2V-5B A100 80GB qualification
claims: The qualification host has one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB and 1TiB installed host memory; CPU offload was not used.
The profile is BF16, batch 1, native FlashAttention, eager mode, VAE tiling, 1280x704, 121 frames, 24fps.
T2V uses 50 steps, guidance 5.0, flow_shift 5.0 and seed 42; I2V uses the same settings.
After warmup, T2V HTTP inference time is 288.267s with observed device peak 27,533MiB; I2V is 299.439s with observed device peak 30,333MiB.
Outputs are H.264 1280x704, 121 frames, 24fps, 5.041667s; the I2V first frame preserves the reference with a reported 5.81 mean absolute pixel error after resize/H.264 encoding.

resources.workflow: vLLM-Omni sync Videos API with VAE tiling

limitations: The host has unusually large 1TiB RAM and no CPU offload; this is a measured qualification but not a L4 or A100-40GB result. Quality was visually inspected rather than scored against a base model.

title: Wan2.2 Accelerate A100 40GB and A100 80GB expected profiles
claims: The guide lists A100 80GB flags --offload_model False, compile reduce-overhead, batched CFG and TF32, with expected 3–3.5x speedup and 100s for 81 frames at 1280x720.
The guide lists A100 40GB flags --offload_model True, compile reduce-overhead, batched CFG and TF32, with expected 2.5–3x speedup and 120s for 81 frames at 1280x720.
The guide labels the A100 timing as expected and documents that its current optimized code is T2V only.
limitations: These are explicitly expected values, not reproducible measurement logs; no host RAM, peak VRAM, scheduler, or quality A/B is supplied.

title: Wan2.2 TI2V-5B GPU Battle benchmark
claims: The benchmark uses Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-Diffusers and a 49-frame 1280x704 workload, single stream, batch size 1.
The page states approximately 18GB VRAM minimum, approximately 34GB for the full path and approximately 38GB system RAM for the workload.
The measured L4 row is 0.15 frames/s at 24GB; the measured A100-SXM4-80GB row is 0.66 frames/s and A100-PCIe-80GB is 0.61 frames/s.
A100-40GB SXM4/PCIe rows are labeled estimated, at 0.66/0.61 frames/s; the page explicitly says estimated rows are interpolated and not run.
The author states the table is based on warmup plus two timed runs, with telemetry sampled at 1Hz; precision is BF16 and no silent precision swap is made.

resources.gpu: L4 24GB measured; A100 40GB rows estimated; A100 80GB measured

limitations: Host RAM is a workload-level statement rather than a per-GPU peak; the page does not provide exact steps, FPS output duration, peak VRAM by row, or video quality metrics. A10040 values are estimates and must remain separate from measured A10080/L4 values.

title: city96 Wan2.1 T2V-14B GGUF
claims: The card says it is a direct GGUF conversion of Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-14B and is intended for ComfyUI-GGUF.
File sizes listed are Q3_K_S 6.99GB, Q3_K_M 7.65GB, Q4_K_S 9.22GB, Q4_K_M 10.1GB, Q5_K_S 10.6GB, Q5_K_M 11.3GB, Q6_K 12.5GB, Q8_0 15.9GB, BF16/F16 29.1GB.
The card does not publish quality, speed, VRAM peak or host RAM comparisons among quant levels.
limitations: File size is not a measured VRAM peak and the card makes no quality ranking claim; no L4/A100 data is supplied.

title: bullerwins Wan2.2 I2V-A14B GGUF
claims: The card requires both a high-noise and a low-noise model; high noise is used for first steps and low noise for detail refinement.
The card requires ComfyUI-GGUF and includes an example workflow.
Each expert is available as Q2_K 5.3GB, Q3_K_S 6.52GB, Q3_K_M 7.18GB, Q3_K_L 7.79GB, Q4_K_S 8.75GB, Q4_K_M 9.65GB, Q5_K_S 10.1GB, Q5_K_M 10.8GB, Q6_K 12GB and Q8_0 15.4GB.
The card contains no controlled quality or low/mid hardware benchmark.

resources.resolution: Wan2.2 I2V supports 480P/720P in the base model
resources.precision: GGUF Q2_K through Q8_0 per high/low expert

limitations: Two file sizes do not equal peak VRAM or host RAM; no L4/A100 output or quality data is reported.

title: Kijai WanVideo_comfy card
claims: Kijai describes the CausVid LoRAs as experimental extractions from CausVid finetunes intended to transfer distillation benefits, not to provide actual causal inference.

Kijai states V1 is a direct extraction with adverse motion effects and flashing at full strength; V1.5 removes the first block; V2 keeps attention layers, fixes flashing and retains motion better but needs more steps and can benefit from CFG.
The card links Wan2.1 CausVid, CFG/step-distill and other Wan acceleration sources.

resources.precision: LoRA extraction variants; quantized files in linked repositories
resources.workflow: ComfyUI native WanVideo nodes or Kijai WanVideoWrapper

limitations: The card does not give L4/A100 measurements; quality statements are author caveats, not a same-seed benchmark.

title: Kijai wrapper issue on direct Wan2.1/Wan2.2 LoRA extraction
claims: An issue participant reports attempting Wan2.2 LoRA extraction for Wan2.1 and seeing layer warnings.
Kijai says a quick direct attempt did not work and suggests the LoRA was probably not trained directly from Wan2.1.
Another participant says LightX2V LoRAs work because Wan2.2 was trained from Wan2.1 with extended training; this is a participant explanation, not a universal compatibility guarantee.
limitations: This is an issue discussion with no reproducible same-seed quality benchmark; it preserves conflicting reports rather than resolving all LoRA compatibility cases.

title: Third-party Wan2.2 T2V A14B NF4 Diffusers card
claims: The card labels the artifact as Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers NF4, 4-bit precision, bitsandbytes and WanPipeline, based on Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers.
The card does not publish a measured GPU, VRAM peak, host RAM, timing or visual-quality comparison for the NF4 artifact.
limitations: NF4 is a third-party packaging/quantization artifact; the card has no low/mid resource test or quality claim. It should not be ranked against GGUF, FP8-scaled or INT8 from labels alone.

title: Wan2.2 Colab wrapper hardware routing
claims: The notebook README routes T4/L4 to TI2V-5B and recommends A100 80GB for A14B.
The README lists approximately 10GB download for TI2V-5B and approximately 28GB for A14B checkpoints.
It states A14B uses offload_model, convert_model_dtype and t5_cpu flags to reduce VRAM and TI2V-5B is the fallback for 24GB cards.

resources.gpu: T4/L4 for TI2V-5B; A100 80GB recommended for A14B

limitations: This source provides routing and model download sizes, not measured L4/A100 time, VRAM peak, host RAM, or visual quality.

title: Wan2Lab TI2V-5B live hardware record
claims: On AMD gfx1200 with 17,095,983,104 bytes reported VRAM, a 5-frame 1280x704 24fps four-step prompt smoke render took 90.26s and I2V took 97.52s.
A full 121-frame 1280x704 24fps render using 1 step completed in 21m13s after VAE tiling; sampling was 4m50s and VAE decode 16m8s.
The wrapper-default VAE tile path OOMed at 16GB; 128-pixel tiles with 64-pixel stride completed, with possible tile seam/quality tradeoff explicitly noted.
The record gives model component file sizes: scaled FP8 transformer 5.28GB, Wan2.2 VAE 1.41GB and UMT5 FP8 6.73GB.

resources.precision: Scaled FP8 transformer/text encoder; BF16 VAE; FP32 VAE launch flag

limitations: The GPU is AMD and below the requested NVIDIA L4/A100 categories; smoke tests explicitly do not constitute visual-quality acceptance and full-length evidence used one step plus aggressive VAE tiling.

title: vLLM-Omni feature compatibility GPU count constraints
claims: The total GPU count must equal ulysses_degree times ring_degree times cfg_parallel_size times tensor_parallel_size.
VAE patch parallelism reuses the DiT process group and cannot exceed its size.
limitations: Used by main to classify WAN11 as multi-GPU. WAN11 itself states model of GPU and parallel degrees but not an explicit device count.
